import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_91/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_91/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_91/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source3_91_1 and Source3_91_2 on 'user_id'
join_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2[['user_id', 'age']], on='user_id', how='left')

# Step 2: Join the above result with Source3_91_0 on 'movie_id'
# Source0 has 'title' and 'video_release_date' columns needed
final_join = pd.merge(join_1_2, source0[['movie_id', 'title', 'video_release_date']], on='movie_id', how='left')

# Reorder columns to match target schema:
# ['title': string, 'movie_id': integer, 'video_release_date': float, 'user_id': float, 'rating': float, 'unix_timestamp': float, 'age': float]

# Ensure correct dtypes:
final_join['title'] = final_join['title'].astype(str)
final_join['movie_id'] = final_join['movie_id'].astype(int)
final_join['video_release_date'] = pd.to_numeric(final_join['video_release_date'], errors='coerce')
final_join['user_id'] = final_join['user_id'].astype(float)
final_join['rating'] = final_join['rating'].astype(float)
final_join['unix_timestamp'] = final_join['unix_timestamp'].astype(float)
final_join['age'] = final_join['age'].astype(float)

# Select and reorder columns exactly as target schema
Target3_91 = final_join[['title', 'movie_id', 'video_release_date', 'user_id', 'rating', 'unix_timestamp', 'age']]

# Write the result to the specified path
Target3_91.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_91/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_91/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_91/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_91/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_91_1 and Source3_91_2 on user_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join Source3_91_0 and the above join on movie_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns that are unique or near unique in target:
# According to target schema and hints, group by title (string), movie_id (int), video_release_date (float but kept as group key because it is in target schema and often NaN), user_id (float but used as group key because it is unique per user)
# However, video_release_date is float and often NaN, so safer to group by title, movie_id, user_id only.
# But target examples show video_release_date is NaN mostly, so include it in group by to keep schema consistent.
# Aggregations: mean for rating, unix_timestamp, age (all floats)
grouped = joined_all.groupby(
    ["title", "movie_id", "video_release_date", "user_id"], dropna=False, as_index=False
).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "unix_timestamp": "mean",
    "age": "mean"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = grouped[["title", "movie_id", "video_release_date", "user_id", "rating", "unix_timestamp", "age"]]

# Write output
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_91/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
